title: A clinical trial of bomedemstat in participants with polycythemia vera (MK-3543-025)
official: A Phase 2/3, randomized, open-label, active-comparator-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of bomedemstat (MK-3543) versus best available therapy in participants with polycythemia vera who have an inadequate response to or are intolerant to hydroxyurea
summary: Main objective: 1.  To compare the clinicohematologic response in participants treated with bomedemstat versus BAT
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Has confirmed local diagnosis of polycythemia vera (PV) per World Health Organization (WHO) diagnostic criteria for PV
2. Participants must be able to swallow oral medication and follow instructions for at home dosing of bomedemstat
3. Must have discontinued prior cytoreductive therapy for condition under study for protocol specified duration
4. Has failed at least one prior line of cytoreductive therapy to lower hematocrit
5. Has a history of inadequate response, resistance to, or intolerant to hydroxyurea (HU) per protocol specified criteria
6. Has no evidence of splenomegaly and no symptoms attributable to splenomegaly, including early satiety, left upper quadrant discomfort, or splenic pain
7. Has locally assessed bone marrow (BM) fibrosis score of Grade 0 or Grade 1 as per modified version of the European Consensus Criteria for Grading Myelofibrosis
8. Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV)-infected participants have well controlled HIV on antiretroviral therapy (ART)
9. Participants who are Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) positive are eligible if they have received Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) antiviral therapy for at least 4 weeks and have undetectable HBV viral load
10. Participants with history of Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) infection are eligible if HCV viral load is undetectable
Exclusion criteria:
1. Has history of any illness/impairment of gastrointestinal (GI) function that might interfere with drug absorption
2. Has evidence at the time of screening of increased risk of bleeding
3. Has history of malignancy, unless potentially curative treatment has been completed with no evidence of malignancy for 2 years.
4. HIV-infected participants with a history of Kaposi’s sarcoma and/or Multicentric Castleman’s Disease
5. Is currently receiving anticancer therapy
6. Has an active infection requiring systemic therapy
7. Has had major surgical procedure ≤4 weeks before first dose of study intervention or has not recovered from side effects of major surgical procedure
